Rashi on Pesachim 23a:10:1.english: They shall be - “And they shall be an abomination to you” (Leviticus 11:11).

Rashi on Pesachim 23a:11:1.hebrew: ולחזקיה למה לי למכתב לא יאכל ומייתי לכם למישרייה - בשלמא לר' אבהו, לא מצינו לאקשויי בכל הנך דכתיב בהו לא תאכל והדר כתיב בו היתר הנאה — דאיצטריך לא תאכלו לאכילה, ואיצטריך היתירא להנאה. אלא לחזקיה, כיון דסוף סוף שרי ליה רחמנא בהנאה, למה לי קרא דשני בדיבורא וכתב לא יאכל דמשמע הנאה, ואיצטריך לכם למישרייה בהנאה? ליכתוב לא תאכל, ותו לא איצטריך לכם:
Rashi on Pesachim 23a:11:1.english: And according to Ḥizkiya, why do I need [the verse] to write: "It shall not be eaten," and bring "for you" to permit it? - Granted, according to Rabbi Abbahu, we could not raise an objection regarding all those [cases] where it is written "you shall not eat" and then permission for benefit is written with regard to it — for "you shall not eat" was necessary for [the prohibition of] eating, and the permission was necessary for [permitting] benefit. But according to Ḥizkiya, since in the end the Merciful One permits it for benefit, why do I need the verse to change its phrasing and write "it shall not be eaten," which implies [a prohibition of] benefit, and [thereby] require "for you" to permit it for benefit? Let it write "you shall not eat," and "for you" would no longer be necessary!

Rashi on Pesachim 23a:11:2.hebrew: טעמא דידי - דאמינא: לא יאכל משמע הנאה — מהא נפקא לי. ואי לאו האי קרא, דכתיב לא יאכל ותו כתב לכם למישרייה, לא הוה ידענא דלא יאכל איסור הנאה הוא. וכל הנך קראי דהיתר הנאה דכתיבי גבי לא תאכל — הא דרשינהו חזקיה למילתא אחרינא, כדאמרן לעיל: תרומתכם, קצירכם — דכל ישראל:
Rashi on Pesachim 23a:11:2.english: My reason - That which I say, that "it shall not be eaten" implies [a prohibition against] benefit, is derived for me from here. And were it not for this verse, in which it is written "it shall not be eaten" and furthermore it wrote "for you" to permit it, I would not have known that "it shall not be eaten" is a prohibition against benefit. And all those verses permitting benefit that are written regarding "you shall not eat" — behold, Ḥizkiya interpreted them for another matter, as we said above: "your heave-offering" [and] "your harvest" [refer to that] of all of Israel.

Rashi on Pesachim 23a:12:1.hebrew: תמה על עצמך היאך נאסר חמץ בהנאה - דס"ל מותר בהנאה כל שבעה, וכ"ש לאחר הפסח. ופליגא דרבי יהודה, דאמר: חמץ שעבר עליו הפסח אסור בהנאה, לקמן בפירקין (פסחים דף כח:):
Rashi on Pesachim 23a:12:1.english: Be astounded with yourself; how is leavened bread prohibited from benefit - For he holds [that it is] permitted to derive benefit [from it] all seven [days], and all the more so after Passover. And [this] disagrees with [the view of] Rabbi Yehuda, who said [that] leavened bread upon which Passover has passed is prohibited from benefit, later in our chapter (Pesachim 28b).

Rashi on Pesachim 23a:14:1.hebrew: תלתא לך כתיבי - לא יראה לך חמץ, ולא יראה לך שאור בכל גבולך, ועוד קרא אחרינא: ולא יראה לך שאור בכל גבולך שבעת ימים:
Rashi on Pesachim 23a:14:1.english: Three [instances of] “with you” are written - “No leavened bread shall be seen with you, and no leaven shall be seen with you in all your borders” (Exodus 13:7), and another verse [states]: “And no leaven shall be seen with you in all your borders seven days” (Deuteronomy 16:4).

Rashi on Pesachim 23a:14:2.hebrew: וצריכי - דאי כתב שאור, משום דחימוצו קשה, אבל חמץ — אימא מותר; ואי כתב חמץ, משום דראוי לאכילה, אבל שאור, דלא אתי למיכליה — אימא לא עבר עליה. הכי מפרש להו בפ"ק דביצה (דף ז:):
Rashi on Pesachim 23a:14:2.english: And they are necessary - For had [the Torah] written [only] leaven, [one might have thought that this is] because its fermentation is intense, but [as for] leavened bread, say [that it is] permitted; and had it written [only] leavened bread, [one might have thought that this is] because it is fit for eating, but [as for] leaven, which one would not come to eat, say that he does not transgress on its account. Thus [the Gemara] explains them in the first chapter of Beitzah (daf 7b).

Rashi on Pesachim 23a:15:1.english: Let us say [it is parallel to a dispute between] Tannaim - [Namely, regarding] Rabbi Abbahu's [teaching concerning] “You shall not eat”.

Rashi on Pesachim 23a:15:2.english: It may be used for work - [The verse] could have written [this] regarding the fat of a carcass.

Rashi on Pesachim 23a:15:3.hebrew: שיכול - אי לא הוה כתב "לכל", הוה אמינא: למלאכת גבוה יהא מותר — אם צריך למשוח ממנו עורות למלאכת בדק הבית, יהא מותר — דהא מישתרי חלב באכילה לגבי גבוה, למזבח; אבל למלאכת הדיוט יהא אסור, שהרי נאמר בו "לא תאכלו", ואיסור הנאה במשמע. ת"ל "לכל מלאכה":
Rashi on Pesachim 23a:15:3.english: For [I] might [have thought] - If [the verse] had not written "any," I would have said: For the service of the Most High it should be permitted — [such as] if one needs to grease hides with it for the upkeep of the Temple, it should be permitted — for fat is permitted for "consumption" with regard to the Most High, for the altar; but for ordinary use it should be forbidden, since regarding it, it is stated: "You shall not eat," and a prohibition of benefit is implied. [Therefore,] the verse states: "For any work."

Rashi on Pesachim 23a:16:1.hebrew: רבי עקיבא אומר כו' - כלומר, לא הוצרך הכתוב להתיר, דלא הוה ס"ד לאיסור, ולא בא אלא לטהרו מכלל טומאת הבשר ולומר שאין חלב בכלל נבילה, ואינו חושש לטומאה, אלא מותר לישתמש טהרות בעור המשוח בחלב נבילה. ואם לא ריבה לכל מלאכה, הייתי אומר: למלאכת הדיוט, להשתמש בו חולין — יהא טהור; אבל למלאכת גבוה, להשתמש קדשים — יהא טמא:
Rashi on Pesachim 23a:16:1.english: Rabbi Akiva says, etc. - That is to say, the verse was not needed to permit [benefit], as it would not have entered [one's] mind that it was forbidden; and it came only to declare it pure from the category of the impurity of meat, and to state that fat is not included in [the impurity of a] carcass, and one need not be concerned about impurity; rather, it is permitted to use [ritually] pure items with leather smeared with the fat of a carcass. And had [the verse] not amplified [the scope by stating] “for any service,” I would have said: For common use, to use it [for] non-sacred items, it shall be pure; but for sacred use, to use [it for] consecrated items, it shall be impure.

Rashi on Pesachim 23a:1:1.hebrew: לרבים - לצורך רבים, כגון באמצע הדרך, לכל עובר:
Rashi on Pesachim 23a:1:1.english: For the public - For the needs of the public, such as in the middle of the road, for any passerby.

Rashi on Pesachim 23a:2:1.hebrew: ונטעתם ליחיד משמע - דאין דרך רבים לנטוע, ולכל חד וחד קאמר ונטעתם:
Rashi on Pesachim 23a:2:1.english: “And you shall plant” indicates [that it applies to] an individual - For it is not the way of many [people] to plant [together], and to each and every one [the verse] says, “And you shall plant.”

Rashi on Pesachim 23a:3:1.hebrew: מערבין לנזיר - עירוב תחומין ביין. אע"פ שסעודה שאינה ראויה לו היא, הואיל ואי מתשיל אנזירותיה שריא ליה — מערבין. וכן לישראל בתרומה — דאי בעי מיתשל עליה, דתרומת טעות אינה תרומה, והדרא לטיבלה, והדר מפריש עלה מינה ובה:
Rashi on Pesachim 23a:3:1.english: One may establish an eiruv on behalf of a nazirite - [This refers to] an eiruv techumin with wine. Even though it is a meal that is not suitable for him, since if he asks [for dissolution] of his naziriteship it becomes permitted to him, one may establish an eiruv [with it]. And likewise for an Israelite with teruma: for if he wishes, he can ask [for dissolution] concerning it, as mistaken teruma is not teruma, and it reverts to its untithed state, and he can then separate [teruma] for it from it and within it.

Rashi on Pesachim 23a:4:1.hebrew: תרומתכם - "ונחשב לכם תרומתכם" — ובתרומת מעשר דמפרשי לוים כתיב. ותרומה גדולה איתקש בההוא קרא, כדכתיב: "כדגן מן הגורן", דהיינו תרומה גדולה:
Rashi on Pesachim 23a:4:1.english: Your teruma - [This refers to the verse:] “And your teruma shall be reckoned unto you” — and it is written regarding terumat ma’aser, which the Levites separate. And teruma gedolah was equated [with it] in that verse, as it is written: “As the grain of the threshing floor,” which is teruma gedolah.

Rashi on Pesachim 23a:4:2.hebrew: ואידך - חזקיה, דאמר "לא תאכלו" לא משמע הנאה — האי "תרומתכם" לאו למישרי הנאה אתא, אלא "תרומתכם" דכל ישראל קאמר, ואורחיה דקרא לאישתעויי הכי. "ישראל" לאו דוקא, דהא בלוים כתיב:
Rashi on Pesachim 23a:4:2.english: And the other - Ḥizkiya, who says that “You shall not eat” does not imply [a prohibition of] benefit — this [phrase] “your teruma” did not come to permit benefit, but rather it means “your teruma” of all Israel, and it is the way of Scripture to speak this way. [The Gemara’s mention of] “Israel” is not exact, as it is written concerning the Levites.

Rashi on Pesachim 23a:6:1.hebrew: גידולו - שיער שלו אסור בהנאה וטעון שריפה, כדכתיב: ״ונתן על האש אשר תחת זבח השלמים״:
Rashi on Pesachim 23a:6:1.english: Its growth - His hair is forbidden for [deriving] benefit and requires burning, as it is written: “And he shall put [it] on the fire that is under the sacrifice of the peace offerings.”

Rashi on Pesachim 23a:6:2.hebrew: מידי ואין דבר אחר כתיב - דילמא גידולו, והוא הדין לדבר אחר, דמאי מיעוט כתב הכא:
Rashi on Pesachim 23a:6:2.english: Is it written: "And no other thing"? - Perhaps [the verse specifies] its growth, and the same law applies to other things [as well], for what exclusion is written here?

Rashi on Pesachim 23a:7:2.hebrew: קוצר לשחת - אע"ג דכתיב: "עומר ראשית קצירכם אל הכהן", דמשמע דאסור לקצור לפני העומר — מותר לקצור לשחת כשהוא עשב, דלאו קציר הוא:
Rashi on Pesachim 23a:7:2.english: One may harvest for fodder - Even though it is written: “The omer, the first of your harvest, to the priest,” which implies that it is forbidden to harvest before the omer, it is permitted to harvest for fodder when it is [still] grass, as it is not [considered] a harvest.

Rashi on Pesachim 23a:7:3.hebrew: ומאכיל לבהמה - אף חיטין גמורין על ידי קיטוף. מכל מקום, חדש מותר בהנאה:
Rashi on Pesachim 23a:7:3.english: And feeds it to an animal - [This includes] even fully ripe wheat, by means of plucking. In any case, new grain is permitted for benefit.

Rashi on Pesachim 23a:8:1.hebrew: ואידך - חזקיה, דלא נפקא ליה הנאה מ״לא תאכלו״, ולא איצטריך ״קצירכם״ למישרי — אמר לך: ״קצירכם״ — דכל ישראל קאמר, ואורחיה דקרא לאישתעויי הכי:
Rashi on Pesachim 23a:8:1.english: And the other - [This is] Ḥizkiya, who does not derive [a prohibition of] benefit from “you shall not eat,” and did not need “your harvest” to permit [benefit. He could] say to you: “Your harvest” means that of all of Israel, and it is the way of Scripture to speak in this manner.

Rashi on Pesachim 23a:9:1.hebrew: שנזדמנו - דווקא שנזדמנו, דלא מצרכינן להו להפקירן; אבל לכתחלה אסור לחזר אחריהן, כדתנן התם במס' שביעית (פ"ז מ"ג): אין עושין סחורה לא בנבילות וטריפות, ולא בשקצים ורמשים:
Rashi on Pesachim 23a:9:1.english: Happen to catch - Specifically [in a case where] they happened [to catch them], for we do not require them to declare them ownerless; but at the outset, it is forbidden to seek after them, as we learned there in Tractate Shevi'it (7:3): “One may not engage in commerce with carcasses or tereifot, nor with creeping and swarming creatures.”

Tosafot on Pesachim 23a:10:1.hebrew: אמר קרא יהיו בהוייתן יהו - וא"ת: א"כ, סוסים וחמורים היכי זבנינן? וי"ל, דבמידי דאכילה מיירי דווקא. ובירושלמי דמסכת שביעית ספ"ח פריך: והרי חמור וגמל? ומשני: למלאכתן הן גדילים. וא"ת: דאמרי' במרובה (ב"ק פב: ושם) אסור לישראל לגדל חזירים — תיפוק ליה דמדאורייתא אסור! וי"ל, דנפקא מינה למיקם בארור. אי נמי, הא דאסור מדאורייתא — היינו להשתכר ולמכור לנכרי לאכול, אבל להשתכר בשומנן או בעורן — לא; או שמגדל שלא למכור אלא למשוח ולהדליק — אפילו הכי בחזירים אסור. א"נ, בנזדמנו לו, כגון שנפלו בירושה — אין לגדלן:
Tosafot on Pesachim 23a:10:1.english: The verse stated: "They shall be" — they shall be as they are - And if you say: If so, how do we buy horses and donkeys? And one can say: It is dealing specifically with items [designated for] food. And in the Yerushalmi of Tractate Shevi'it, at the end of chapter 8, it asks: "And behold, a donkey and a camel [are non-kosher, yet one may purchase them]?" And it answers: "They are raised for their labor." And if you say: That which we say in [the chapter entitled] Merubah (Bava Kamma 82b, and elsewhere): "It is forbidden for an Israelite to raise pigs" — let it be derived from the fact that it is forbidden by Torah law! And one can say: The practical difference is to be subject to [the curse of] "cursed." Alternatively: That which is forbidden by Torah law is to profit and sell [them] to a gentile to eat, but to profit from their fat or from their hide is not [forbidden by Torah law]; or where one raises [them] not to sell, but rather to smear [with their fat] and to kindle [lamps] — even so, in the case of pigs, it is forbidden. Alternatively: In a case where they happened upon him, such as where they fell [to him] as an inheritance, one may not raise them.

Tosafot on Pesachim 23a:12:1.hebrew: שאני התם דאמר קרא לא יראה לך - תימה: דליכתב "לא יאכל" לחזקיה, ולא בעי "לך":
Tosafot on Pesachim 23a:12:1.english: "It is different there, as the verse said: '[It] shall not be seen with you'" - [This is] puzzling: for let [the Torah] write "It shall not be eaten" according to Ḥizkiya, and it would not need "[with] you"!

Tosafot on Pesachim 23a:1:1.hebrew: נטוע לרבים - ברה"י, לצורך רבים; ולא כמו שפ"ה: "באמצע הדרך". דקתני במסכת ערלה (פ"א מ"ב): "הנוטע לרבים — חייב, ורבי יהודה פוטר", והדר קתני: "הנוטע ברה"ר, והנכרי שנטע, והגזלן" כו'. מדקתני בתרי בבי, ש"מ תרי מילי נינהו:
Tosafot on Pesachim 23a:1:1.english: Planted for the public - [This means it was planted] in a private domain for the need of the public, and not as the Kuntres [Rashi] explained: "in the middle of the road." For it is taught in tractate Orlah (1:2): "One who plants for the public is obligated, and Rabbi Yehuda exempts," and then it teaches: "One who plants in the public domain, and a gentile who planted, and a robber..." etc. From [the fact] that it teaches [them] in two [separate] clauses, learn from this that they are two [different] matters.

Tosafot on Pesachim 23a:3:1.hebrew: מערבין לנזיר ביין - בפ' בכל מערבין (עירובין כח.) מפרש טעמא: משום דאע"ג דלא חזי להאי, חזי להאי. ולא פריך הכא אליבא דמ"ד (שם דף לא.): "אין מערבין אלא לדבר מצוה", ומצות לאו ליהנות ניתנו:
Tosafot on Pesachim 23a:3:1.english: One may establish an eiruv on behalf of a nazirite with wine - In the chapter [entitled] B'khol Me'arvin (Eruvin 28a), [the Gemara] explains the reason: because even though it is not fit for this [person], it is fit for that [person]. And [the Gemara] does not ask here according to the one who says (ibid. 31a): "One may establish an eiruv only for the purpose of a mitzvah," and mitzvot were not given for benefit.

Tosafot on Pesachim 23a:5:1.hebrew: נזרו שלו יהא - תימה: לחזקיה, "נזרו" למאי אתא? ואית ספרים דגרסינן: "על נזרו מגלח, ואינו מגלח על נזירות אביו":
Tosafot on Pesachim 23a:5:1.english: “His naziriteship” — it shall be his - [This is] puzzling: According to Ḥizkiya, what does “his naziriteship” come [to teach]? And there are books in which we read: “He shaves for his [own] naziriteship, but does not shave for his father's naziriteship.”

Tosafot on Pesachim 23a:7:1.hebrew: קוצר לשחת ומאכיל לבהמה - אף על גב דהא דקוצר לשחת היינו דווקא לבהמה, כדמוכח במנחות בפ' רבי ישמעאל (מנחות ד' עא:) — מ"מ "ומאכיל לבהמה" לא משמע ליה דקאי אקוצר לשחת; דא"כ, לא פריך מידי, דחדש שאסר הכתוב היינו תבואה גמורה. אלא "מאכיל לבהמה" היינו אפילו חיטין גמורין ועל ידי קיטוף, כפ"ה. ועוד, דקתני סיפא: "רבי שמעון אומר: יקצור ויאכל אף משהביא שליש":
Tosafot on Pesachim 23a:7:1.english: "One harvests for fodder and feeds to an animal" - Even though the fact that one harvests for fodder is specifically for an animal, as is proven in Menachot in the chapter [entitled] "Rabbi Yishmael" (Menachot 71b) — nevertheless, "and feeds to an animal" did not indicate to [the Gemara] that it refers [back] to "one harvests for fodder"; for if so, it would not be posing any challenge, for the chadash [new grain] that Scripture forbade is [only] fully grown grain. Rather, "and feeds to an animal" means even fully grown wheat, and via [hand-]plucking, as explained by the Kuntres [Rashi]. And furthermore, as the latter clause [of that Mishnah] teaches: "Rabbi Shimon says: One may harvest and feed even once it has reached a third [of its growth]."

Tosafot on Pesachim 23a:8:1.hebrew: קצירכם שלכם יהא - תימה לרשב"א: מנ"ל דאתא להכי? הא איצטריך לכדדרשינן במנחות בפרק ר' ישמעאל (מנחות דף עב. ושם): "קצירכם" — ולא קציר מצוה! וחזקיה נמי, לישני הכי? וי"ל: מדלא כתב "ראשית קציר", והוי מצי למיכתב "קצירך", וכתב "קצירכם" — שמע מינה תרתי:
Tosafot on Pesachim 23a:8:1.english: “Your harvest” — it shall be yours - It is puzzling to the Rashba: From where do we know that it comes for this [purpose]? Behold, it was needed for that which we expound in Menachot in the chapter [entitled] Rabbi Yishmael (Menachot 72a, and there): “'Your harvest' — and not the harvest of a mitzvah”! And let Ḥizkiya also answer this? And one can say: Since it did not write “the first of the harvest,” and it could have written “your harvest” [in the singular], yet it wrote “your harvest” [in the plural] — deduce two things from it.
